device: AT-X (iPhone 15 Pro Max, A17 Pro), iOS 26.6
purpose: First-ever energy and memory measurement for this project, any model, any semester (see paper/PAPER_DRAFT_v5.md Section 7.2). Closes the last outstanding gap in the effectiveness scorecard.

method.note_on_process: First real hardware run for this project's scripts/run_physical_device_session.sh, which surfaced and fixed five real bugs in sequence (device-detection false-positive on a simulator, expired provisioning profile not renewed by plain xcodebuild, install path pointing at a stale April build instead of the fresh one, a fragile devicectl-launch+PID-lookup race replaced with xctrace's atomic --launch, and 'Energy Log' being renamed 'Power Profiler' in this Xcode version) -- all committed to the repo as part of the fix, not just worked around ad hoc for this one session.

power_profiler_methodology_note: First attempt for each model was captured while the device was USB-tethered to the Mac (required for xctrace to attach) and therefore actively charging -- confirmed via the 'Charger Connected' track showing active for the full recording, and an uninformative exact 0.0%/hr average power reading as a direct symptom. Re-captured for both models over a Wi-Fi-paired connection with the USB cable physically disconnected, which produced real, non-zero, sub-5%/hr readings for both models. The charging-condition traces are not used for the reported numbers below.

tiny_multimodal_v1.peak_memory_source: Allocations instrument, 'Current Bytes' track peak (NOT the Statistics table's 'Total Bytes' column, which is a lifetime cumulative sum across the whole recording including freed memory and would overstate peak footprint by ~10x)
tiny_multimodal_v1.avg_power_threshold_status: FAIL (target: < 5%/hr) -- narrow, not padded to pass
tiny_multimodal_v1.caveat: Avg power blends ~5-10s of active inference (visible as a sharp CPU/power spike at recording start) with ~37s of near-idle time afterward -- a 'typical session' rate, not a pure continuous-active-inference rate, which would likely be higher.

axiom_lora_v1.peak_memory_source: Allocations instrument, 'Current Bytes' track peak, same methodology as above
axiom_lora_v1.caveat: Same blended-average caveat as tiny_multimodal_v1. A brief ~1s instantaneous peak of 32.8%/hr is visible in the trace during the active-inference burst, well above the 4.8%/hr session average.

honest_finding: Neither model comfortably passes the < 5%/hr energy threshold -- tiny_multimodal_v1 fails narrowly (5.2%), axiom_lora_v1 passes narrowly (4.8%). Both are close enough to the boundary that the 'pass/fail' label is more a function of measurement noise at these small margins than a clear separation between the models. Both pass memory (<500MB target) and latency comfortably, by wide margins established in earlier sessions.
not_measured: axiom_lora_text_v1 has no on-device Swift/CoreML integration in this pass (Python-side train/export/accuracy-gate only, per paper/PAPER_DRAFT_v5.md Section 5.3), so it cannot be profiled on-device this way.
